items.description: South Devon coast from Start Point to Dawlish Warren
items.eaAreaName: Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
items.message:
High tides, strong winds and large waves over the next two days may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from 3 hours either side of high tide on Tuesday afternoon and Wednesday morning.
Areas particularly at risk include Torbay, Teignmouth, Beesands, Torcross, Slapton and Dawlish. The high tide at Teignmouth on Tuesday afternoon is at 18:15, times of high water will vary along the coast. Forecast total high tide level is 2.3mAOD; 0.23 metres above tide table level. Force 5 south easterly winds and wave heights of over 1.5m are forecast over the high tide. 
The high tide on Wednesday morning is at 06:30. Forecast total high tide level is 2.30mAOD; 0.09 metres above tide table level. Force 5 north easterly winds and wave heights of over 1.3m are forecast.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.  
This message will be updated by 2:00PM on Wednesday 25 November or as the situation changes.

Flooding is possible from 16:15 to 20:15 on 24/11/2026.

We are closely monitoring the situation .

items.message:
High river levels today may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from the morning of Tuesday 24 November .
Catchments are saturated and river levels are rising in response to overnight rainfall.  Heavy rain is forecast to continue throughout Tuesday. 

The highest river levels are forecast over Tuesday afternoon and evening, with flooding to riverside and low-lying land and roads expected.
  
Rain is forecast to ease over Tuesday night, with river levels dropping by Wednesday morning.
We are monitoring rainfall and river levels .
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. Monitor local water levels and weather conditions.
This message will be updated by 11:00AM on Wednesday 25 November or as the situation changes.

High tides, strong winds and large waves over the next two days may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 05:15am to 07:15am and 17:45pm to 19:45pm on Wednesday 25th November. 
Locations most affected will be low lying land and roads near rivers or on the coast, with spray being seen on the seafront paths. Flood gates in the area will be closed by the Local Authority which will make access difficult. Please take notice of the Flood Sign at the top of South Beach Road. 
The detailed forecast is for a peak level at  Kings Lynn of 3.81mAODN at 06:15am, on Wednesday 25th November, Wind Force 6, Easterly. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded.  
This message will be updated by 11:00AM on Wednesday 25 November or as the situation changes.

items.description: The tidal Rivers Bure, Ant and Thurne
items.message:
Tide locking, where high tides restrict normal drainage of the river out to sea, over the next two days may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible today, Tuesday 24th November, and tomorrow, Wednesday 25th November.
We expect to see high water levels around Potter Heigham, Wroxham boat yards and Ferry Road in Horning. Levels can take several hours to peak compared to published tide tables.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.  
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on Wednesday 25 November or as the situation changes.

items.description: River Hayle from Relubbus to St Erth
items.eaAreaName: Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
items.message:
Rising river levels are expected to cause flooding overnight. 
Flooding is expected from the evening of Tuesday 24 November and into the morning of Wednesday 25 November. 
Rainfall in the area will continue throughout tonight.

Properties and low lying areas will start to flood from around 17:30pm on Tuesday. The main areas of concern are properties and low lying areas around the bottom of Tregembo Hill, Green Lane, Battery Hill Playground, Chapel Hill and Chenhalls Road. Flood waters may be deep and fast flowing in these areas. 

River levels are forecast to be at their highest overnight into Wednesday morning. 
We are monitoring rainfall and river levels . 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.   
This message will be updated by 11:00AM on Wednesday 25 November or as the situation changes.
